rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a concrete template: it is a nearly contemporaneous Cabinet resignation letter with the same effective date, an opening that accepts the resignation and credits eight years of service, a central catalogue of departmental programs and accomplishments, and a closing wish for future health and happiness. C14 and C24 share much of this machinery, but C13 most closely matches the child's compact progression and phrasing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I accept your resignation as of January 20, 1961... Your report of the accomplishments of your Department during these last eight years
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As Secretary of Agriculture for the past eight years... in accepting your resignation, effective January 20, 1961
shared_material.explanation: Both begin by combining the same resignation date with an appraisal of eight years of Cabinet service.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am particularly impressed that our production of hydroelectric power... [followed by a series of departmental accomplishments]
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Among the vital programs that you have worked for so effectively, these immediately come to mind: The Rural Development Program... the Food for Peace Program... [and other programs]
shared_material.explanation: Both devote the body of the letter to an enumerated catalogue of signature departmental programs and measurable achievements.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In the years ahead, may you always have good health and happiness.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I again thank you and wish you a future life of good health and happiness as you leave government service.
shared_material.explanation: The closings share unusually close language wishing health and happiness after departure from government service.
